newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Mar 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Mar 6.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on March 6:

WASHINGTON - Hillary Rodham Clinton's top aide took a $50,000 political donation from California businessman Johnny Chung while he was visiting the White House in March 1995, even though federal law bars government employees from accepting campaign contributions on federal property.
WASHINGTON - The White House "bully pulpit," President Clinton is learning as he tries to shift the focus off campaign fundraising, isn't quite as effective as it used to be.

BERLIN - In the boldest response yet to accusations that it profited from the Holocaust, Switzerland offered to create a large humanitarian fund that would draw on the country's vast gold reserves to aid victims of catastrophes, human rights abuses and Nazi terror.

WASHINTON - Until the early 1980s, the U.S. military ran an intelligence training programme in Latin America and elsewhere using manuals that taught foreign officers to offer bounties for captured or killed insurgents, spy on non-violent political opponents, kidnap rebels' family members and blackmail unwanted informants.

WASHINGTON - National Institutes of Health director Harold Varmus said that despite the flurry of negative reaction to the idea of cloning human beings, society may at some point decide that human cloning is acceptable under certain conditions.

YOSEMITE NATIONAL PARK, Calif. - They are calling it the cruelest winter on record, but in this great glacial valley the bears, bobcats and coyotes are wandering fat and happy through the abandoned campgrounds and empty parking lots.
WASHINGTON - Efforts to move the poor from welfare to work are moving slowly in the District of Columbia.
